universal_lens: The universal lens unifies streakiness and consistency via the variance of anchored rolling means over binary outcome sequences. By mapping pitch-level outcomes to a sliding window, we construct a stochastic process where deviations from ergodic expectations quantify temporal clustering, bridging combinatorial permutations with continuous volatility metrics.

reasoning_traces.think:
The derivation begins by defining a discrete-time stochastic process representing pitch outcomes. Unlike traditional aggregate statistics, we focus on the micro-structure of these sequences. The anchored rolling mean operator extracts local density of successes, transforming a binary sequence into a continuous trajectory. Streakiness is then mathematically formalized not as a run-length alone, but as the variance of this trajectory. To isolate true skill-based clustering from random noise, we employ permutational inference. By shuffling the observed outcomes, we generate a null distribution of variances assuming memorylessness. The divergence of the empirical variance from this null distribution yields a robust measure of abnormal streakiness. This dual approach—local smoothing followed by global permutation testing—creates a powerful primitive for distinguishing signal from noise in high-frequency sports data. The duality lies in treating consistency as the inverse of this variance, allowing us to rank players on a spectrum from highly volatile to remarkably steady. Failure modes emerge when the window size is poorly calibrated, either masking long-term trends or amplifying short-term noise.
